content.value_statement: Database schema changes can cause downtime, data loss, and rollback gaps. This skill helps plan ORM migrations, data transformations, and verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Shows Sequelize, TypeORM, and Prisma migration patterns.
Outlines additive schema changes and column rename strategies.
Provides examples for data backfills and field transformations.
Explains transaction-based and checkpoint rollback approaches.
Describes blue-green and cross-database migration considerations.
limitations: It does not connect to databases or execute migrations by itself.
Examples are generic and require review for each production schema.
Referenced auxiliary resources and scripts are not included in the scanned package.
It does not replace backups, staging tests, or DBA approval.

use_cases.title: Add Fields Without Downtime
use_cases.description: Plan additive columns, defaults, and phased application changes for safer releases.

use_cases.title: Refactor Application Data Models
use_cases.description: Map schema changes to ORM migrations and data transformation steps.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Rollout Plans
use_cases.description: Define backups, rollback checkpoints, verification queries, and monitoring steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Migration Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small schema change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a database migration to add [field] to [table]. Include the ORM steps, rollback plan, and staging checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare ORM Migration Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before choosing an implementation path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Sequelize, TypeORM, and Prisma approaches for [schema change]. Highlight tradeoffs, risks, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Rollback-Ready Transformation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for data transformation and recovery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reversible migration for transforming [source data] into [target structure]. Include checkpoints, backups, and verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Zero-Downtime Rollout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production deployment with phased application changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a zero-downtime rollout plan for changing [table or column]. Include phases, dual writes, backfill, monitoring, and rollback.

output_examples.input: Add a status field to users without interrupting production traffic.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with an additive column, default handling, staging validation, production monitoring, and a rollback path.

output_examples.input: Move address text into separate street, city, and state fields.
output_examples.output: A transformation outline with parsing rules, data quality checks, batch processing guidance, and recovery checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Rename an email column during a blue-green deployment.
output_examples.output: A rollout sequence covering compatible schema changes, dual-write behavior, backfill verification, and final cleanup.

best_practices: Back up data and test every migration on staging before production.
Prefer small, reversible steps with explicit down migrations.
Monitor locks, latency, errors, and data counts during rollout.
anti_patterns: Running destructive migrations before validating backups and rollback.
Combining unrelated schema and data changes in one deployment.
Changing column types on large tables without phased backfills.

faq.question: Does this skill run database migrations?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and examples. Users must run approved migrations in their own environment.

faq.question: Which ORM tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for Sequelize, TypeORM, and Prisma, plus general SQL migration concepts.

faq.question: Can it help with zero-downtime changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes phased changes, additive columns, backfills, dual-write periods, and cleanup steps.

faq.question: Does it include rollback guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers down migrations, transactions, checkpoints, backups, and restoration planning.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: Use it as planning support only. Production migrations still need backups, staging tests, and operational approval.

faq.question: Can it support cross-database migrations?
faq.answer: It gives dialect-aware considerations, but users must verify data types and behavior for each database engine.
